'''Robert Duncan MacPherson''' (born May 25, 1944) is an American mathematician at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].

== Early life and education ==
Robert Duncan MacPherson was born in [[Lakewood, Ohio]] on May 25, 1944.<ref name="CV"/> He received his bachelor's degree from [[Swarthmore College]] in 1966.<ref name="CV" /> MacPherson then received his PhD from [[Harvard University|Harvard]] in 1970 with a thesis, written under the direction of [[Raoul Bott]], entitled ''Singularities of Maps and Characteristic Classes''.<ref name="MG">{{MathGenealogy|id=11546|title=Robert MacPherson}}</ref>

==Career==
MacPherson was at [[Brown University]] as a J. D. Tamarkin Instructor from 1970 to 1972, an assistant professor from 1972 to 1974, an associate professor from 1974 to 1977, and then a professor from 1977 to 1987.<ref name="CV"/> He was a professor at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] from 1987 to 1994.<ref name="CV"/> He became a professor of mathematics at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in 1994, later becoming named a Hermann Weyl Professor.<ref name="CV"/> He retired and became a professor emeritus 2018.<ref name="CV">{{cite web |url=https://www.ias.edu/sites/default/files/math/rdm/BriefCVMacP.html |website=Robert D. MacPherson |title=Curriculum Vitae |access-date=May 14, 2024}}</ref>

His notable doctoral students include [[Mark Goresky]], [[David Nadler (mathematician)|David Nadler]], [[Julianna Tymoczko]], [[Kari Vilonen]], and [[Zhiwei Yun]].<ref name="MG"/>

==Research==
MacPherson and Goresky introduced [[intersection homology]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Robert D. MacPherson |url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/2012/05/30/robert-d-macpherson/ |website=Simons Foundation}}</ref> He also worked on [[arithmetic group]]s, in particular on [[Siegel modular variety|Siegel modular threefold]]s with Mark McConnell and on [[compactification (mathematics)|compactification]]s of [[symmetric space]]s with [[Lizhen Ji]].<ref>{{cite journal |first=Paul E. |last=Gunnells |journal=Pure and Applied Mathematics Quarterly |volume=2 |year=2006 |issue=4 |title=Robert MacPherson and Arithmetic Groups  |pages=1015–1052 |doi=10.4310/PAMQ.2006.v2.n4.a5|arxiv=math/0603385 }}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
In 1983, MacPherson gave a [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|plenary address]] at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]].

In 1992, MacPherson was awarded the [[NAS Award in Mathematics]] from the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=NASMath>{{cite web|title=NAS Award in Mathematics|url=http://www.nasonline.org/site/PageServer?pagename=AWARDS_mathematics|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060102132528/http://www.nasonline.org/site/PageServer?pagename=AWARDS_mathematics|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 2, 2006|publisher=National Academy of Sciences|accessdate=February 13, 2011}}</ref> In 2002, he and Goresky were awarded the [[Leroy P. Steele Prize]] for Seminal Contribution to Research by the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200204/comm-steeleprz.pdf|title=Notices of the AMS 2002 p. 466|website=ams.org}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/prizes-awards/pabrowse?purl=steele-prize?SCR|title=List of Steele Prizes Seminal Contribution to Research|website=www.ams.org}}</ref> In 2009 he received the [[Heinz Hopf Prize]] from [[ETH Zurich]].<ref name="CV"/>

In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved February 2, 2013.</ref> He is also a fellow of the National Academy of Sciences and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref name="CV"/>

He received honorary doctorates from the [[University of Lille]] in 1993 and [[Brown University]] in 1994.<ref name="CV"/>

== Personal ==
MacPherson's PhD advisee, Mark Goresky, later became his life partner.<ref name=":0"/> After the collapse of the Soviet Union, they were instrumental in channeling aid to Russian mathematicians, especially many who had to hide their sexuality.<ref name=":0" />

==Selected publications==
* Goresky, Mark; MacPherson, Robert, ''La dualité de Poincaré pour les espaces singuliers'', C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris Sér. A-B 284 (1977), no. 24, A1549–A1551.  {{MathSciNet|id=0440533}}
* Goresky, Mark; MacPherson, Robert,  ''Intersection homology theory'', [[Topology (journal)|Topology]] 19 (1980), no. 2, 135–162. {{doi|10.1016/0040-9383(80)90003-8}} {{MathSciNet|id=0572580}}
* Goresky, Mark; MacPherson, Robert, ''Intersection homology. II'', [[Inventiones Mathematicae]] 72 (1983), no. 1, 77–129. {{doi|10.1007/BF01389130}} {{MathSciNet|id=0696691}}
